AUTHOR: Cutter
TITLE: Automated Detection of Rockfish in Unconstrained Underwater Videos Using Haar Cascades and a New Image Dataset: Labeled Fishes in the Wild
REGION: Southern California Bight, USA (NOAA ROV rockfish surveys 2000-2012)
SPECIES: Groundfishes, mainly rockfishes (Sebastes spp.); detected as generic 'fish'
DATA: Own ROV footage released as 'Labeled Fishes in the Wild' (929 training stills with 1005 fish; 211-frame test video with 2061 fish objects; 3167 negative images incl. 3020 OpenCV tutorial images)
V_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'they tend to first appear in the dimly lit distance ... the fishes' colors change because of the rapid attenuation of light in seawater'; no quantitative visibility measure, no stratified results
D2: 929 training/validation stills vs. one independent 211-frame test video (no separate validation set; validation set included training images)
D_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'the dataset also includes an independent test image set that represents images as they are collected by the moving platform in the ocean'
R_EV: Sec. 3.1: test set 'contains an image sequence collected using the ROV's video camera during a near-seabed survey of fish'
C_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'higher TPs (e.g. 82 to 85%) could be achieved by increasing the allowed difference ... but at the expense of higher FPs (8.5 to 12.3)'
E_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'detection performance using the Haar cascade classifiers ranged from 63% to 89% true positive detection rate'; only TP/FA/FP rates reported, no ecological variable
ARCH: Haar-like feature cascade classifiers (Viola-Jones, AdaBoost), OpenCV 2.4.8 haartraining/traincascade; detector in C# .NET + Accord.NET
METR: True positive detection rate, false alarm count, false positive rate (TP vs FA curves)
NOTE: Classical ML (Haar cascades), no CNN. 'Validation set' included training images, so only the test video is a true held-out set; split is by footage source (stills vs. one test video), coded as 영상(video). Detector operating points are cascade stages/MHR/SFA and 'detected at least twice' suppression rather than a confidence threshold (C1 coded Y on that basis). Visibility only described qualitatively (light attenuation, dim distance, particles); 'range to target' named as a performance factor but not quantified. ENV coded as temperate rocky seabed; merged.json lists 'deep sea' - verifier should decide. E4=FNR derived from reported TP rate (recall); no size-class analysis.
